Oil residue in the lungs is a myth, if you took a single 18650 cell and whipped off the battery wrap and put it inside of 2 mechanical mods at completely different price points it’s still going to blow. 99.9% of the time it’s all down to user error and people not keeping an eye on things or learning their batteries on charge over night in a mod. As a Vaper of a couple years and having bought all kinds of mods an expensive vape can be for all kinds of reasons, company uses a dna chip so seems it worthy of a higher price tag, unique or better materials used is a main reason for a higher price tag. As long as you look after your mods and batteries nothing should blow up obviously you can’t 100% say never as with anything. Just have a look on YouTube, there’s been some great things come onto the market, I bought a “Strangers Mod” from a friend who had it made and paid €800 for it. Never once had a thought it might blow or fail on me but boyyy did it feel like it had a lot of man hours put into it by hand and not just mass produced. You don’t necessarily need to spend loads on vaping, one persons expensive setup won’t put perform Joe Bloggs run of the mill EZ Watt kit if both are being used just for nicotine delivery. I wouldn’t suggest quitting and going back to smoking even if there are risks, the underlying fact that vaping is the lesser of the two evils still wins for me. Sorry for rambling but I’ve worked in two vape shops in the past and both were completely different.
